title: Misleading comment about METHOD_CORR in test_edhoc.py
description:
File: python/tests/crypto/test_edhoc.py
Line 392

The parametrized test vector comment says:
  _sequence(4, 0, b"x" * 32, b"\x00"),  # method_corr=4 -> method=1 (unsupported)

This comment is misleading. RFC 9528 deprecated METHOD_CORR (which existed in earlier drafts). In RFC 9528, the first value is simply METHOD, which must be 0-3. A value of 4 is just an invalid METHOD value, not a METHOD_CORR encoding.

The test WORKS correctly (the implementation rejects METHOD=4), but the comment confuses readers about the EDHOC protocol and may lead to incorrect assumptions about message encoding.

Fix: Change comment to:
  _sequence(4, 0, b"x" * 32, b"\x00"),  # method=4 (invalid, valid range 0-3)
